title: Meet a part of you
subtitle: You write both voices. The app holds the space.

steps.body:
Before you begin.

You're about to sit with a part of yourself — maybe one you've kept at arm's length for a long time.

The conversation goes at your pace. You can stop whenever you need to. Nothing here will push you further than you want to go.
Take a breath. Let yourself arrive here.
Ready to begin? You can also stop here — this will be waiting when you are.

steps.title: What brings you here today?
steps.body: Both paths are real work. Neither is harder or more important than the other.

options.label: Meet something you've admired from afar

steps.title: How are you walking in?
steps.body: Just a baseline before we begin. No right answer.

steps.title: What would you call this part?
steps.body: Not a clinical name — just the one that fits. The Critic. The one who shuts down. Whatever comes.
steps.placeholder: A name or a few words…

steps.title: If this part had a face, a body, a shape — what do you see?
steps.body: Let an image arrive. You don't have to analyze it — just describe what appears.

steps.title: How old does it feel?
steps.body: Parts sometimes carry the age they first appeared. It might be a number, or just a sense — young, old, ancient.

steps.title: Where do you feel this in your body?
steps.body: Chest, throat, gut, shoulders — wherever the sensation lives.

steps.title: When do you first remember this part showing up?
steps.body: It might be an age, a situation, a person who was there. Or just a feeling — early, recent, always.

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let this part speak. Write as it — not about it. What does it want to say first?
steps.hint: If you already know what it's going to say, you might be steering. Aim to surprise yourself.

steps.speaker: you
steps.prompt: Your turn. Write your response — what do you say back to it?

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Ask it: what are you protecting? Write its answer in its own words.

steps.speaker: you
steps.prompt: Stay with what it told you. What comes up in you?

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let it tell you what it wants. Not what it's supposed to want — what it actually wants.

steps.title: What does this part need from you?
steps.body: Not a resolution — just one honest thing. It might be small. It might be something you've never offered it before.

steps.title: Who do you admire to the point of ache?
steps.body: An artist, a person, a character — real or invented. The one whose work or presence stops you.

steps.title: What quality is that?
steps.body: Not what they do — the thing underneath it. Their directness? Their ease? The way they take up space?

steps.title: When did you decide that quality wasn't allowed to be yours?
steps.body: You don't have to find a specific moment. Sometimes it's a feeling — that it would be too much, or not enough, or that it wasn't safe.

steps.title: Where could a little of it live this week?
steps.body: Something small, something real. Not a transformation — just one place where this quality gets to exist.

steps.title: How are you right now?
steps.body: After sitting with something, the charge sometimes shifts. Just notice where you are.

exit.body: That's enough for today. Whatever came up, it came up for a reason.
